#### List:

- Intro
- PC
- PK
- PD

#### Intro:

- Used as a sole agent in 3^rd^ world and field anaesthesia
- Anaesthetic: for induction (bolus) and maintenance (infusion or repeat boluses)
- Analgesic
- Relatively safe cardiovascular and respiratory profile
- Cheap

#### Pharmaceutics:

- Stable in solution
- No toxic additives (benzethonium chloride: theoretical risk neurotoxicity)
- Low risk of bacterial growth
- No bacterial growth
- No histamine release
- No anaphylaxis
- No pain on IV injection
- Suitable for IM injection of IV access lost

#### Pharmacokinetics:

+----------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Administration | - Many routes: IV, IM, SC, intranasal, PO                          |
|                | - Used for oral premedication in children                          |
|                | - For IM sedation of patients without IV access                    |
+----------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Time course    | - Fast onset (30 seconds)                                          |
|                | - Fast peak (90 seconds)                                           |
|                | - Duration highly dependent upon dose                              |
+----------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Absorption     | N/A                                                                |
+----------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Distribution   | - Very high lipid solubility (5-10x that of thiopentone)           |
|                | - Very fast effect site equilibration (t~1/2ke0~ 0.5 minutes)      |
|                |   - Suitable for induction                                         |
|                | - Large V~DSS~ 3L/kg                                               |
|                | - Rapid distribution                                               |
|                |   - Can be rapid offset after a bolus                              |
+----------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Metabolism     | - Hepatic, phase 1, CYP3A4 N-demethylation \> other                |
|                | - High hepatic extraction ratio, flow-dependent clearance          |
|                | - Subject to induction and inhibition                              |
|                | - Active metabolite norketamine (30% as active)                    |
|                |   - May increase duration of effect                                |
|                |   - Inactivated by hydroxylation then conjugation                  |
|                |   - t~1/2~~β~ 4 hours                                              |
|                | - Rapid clearance 17mL/kg/min and short t~1/2~~β~ 2 hours          |
|                |   - Suitable for maintenance infusion                              |
|                | - Can be hepatotoxic                                               |
+----------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Excretion      | - Active metabolite renally excreted; accumulates in renal failure |
+----------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### CNS effect:

+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Mechanisms               | - Principal: non-competitive NMDA antagonist at PCP site                                   |
|                          | - Other ↑: 2PK/5HT~3~/mu opioid                                                            |
|                          | - Other ↓: VDNaC, VdCC, monoamine reuptake, nnAChR                                         |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Anaesthesia              | - Thalamocortical dissocation (amnesia, sedation, hypnosis, immobility; not anxiolytic)    |
|                          | - Atypical effect on EEG; not suitable for BIS or entropy monitoring                       |
|                          | - S-ketamine more potent than R-ketamine                                                   |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Other beneficial effects | - Analgesia:                                                                               |
|                          |   - Multiple mechanisms (↓NMDA, ↑monoamines, ↑↓opioids, VDNaC)                             |
|                          |   - ↓Acute and chronic pain                                                                |
|                          |   - ↓Somatic and neuropathic                                                               |
|                          |   - ↓Hyperalgaesia and allodynia                                                           |
|                          |   - Opioid-sparing\                                                                        |
|                          |     \                                                                                      |
|                          | - Anaesthesia + analgesia allows use as a sole agent (e.g. field anaesthesia, 3^rd^ world) |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Side effects             | - Emergence delirium:                                                                      |
|                          |   - R-ketamine \> S-ketamine                                                               |
|                          |   - Hallucinations, nightmares in 30%                                                      |
|                          |   - Higher risk if psychiatric illness                                                     |
|                          |   - ?Attenuated by midazolam                                                               |
|                          | - Emetogenic                                                                               |
|                          | - ↑CMRO2, ↑CBF +/- ↑ICP                                                                    |
|                          |   - Contraindicated if CNS bleed or tumour with ↑ICP                                       |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Unclear effects          | - Both pro- and anti-convulsant                                                            |
|                          | - Neurotoxic to the developing brain; but may attenuate excitotoxicity in HIBI             |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Cardiovascular:

+-----------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Direct effects  | - R-ketamine \> S-ketamine                                                           |
|                 | - Negative inotropy, venodilatation, vasodilatation                                  |
+-----------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Indirect effect | - ↑SNS output from medulla                                                           |
|                 |   - ↑HR, ↑contractility, ↑SVR                                                        |
|                 |   - ↑MVO2 → risk myocardial ischaemia                                                |
|                 |   - ↑PVR → ↑RV strain (avoid ↓PaO~2~, ↑PaCO~2~)                                      |
|                 | - Direct effects balance indirect effects in health                                  |
|                 | - Negative inotropy may be unmasked if maximal SNS activity or high dose vasoactives |
|                 | - Baroreceptor reflex relatively preserved                                           |
+-----------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Respiratory:

+--------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    | - Thalamocortical dissociation with relative preservation of vital medullary activity |
|                    | - ↑SNS output and ↓L-Ca^2+^ → smooth muscle relaxation                                |
+--------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Beneficial effects | - Preserved ventilation (↔RR, TV), airway reflexes and pharyngeal dilator tone        |
|                    | - Preserved airway reflexes                                                           |
|                    | - Preserved pharyngeal dilator tone                                                   |
|                    | - R-ketamine→ bronchodilation (suitable induction agent in status asthmaticus)        |
|                    | - Ideal for field anaesthesia or if limited resources                                 |
|                    | - May be inadequate alone for airway instrumentation                                  |
+--------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Side effects       | - ↑Airway secretion (may need anti-sialogogue)                                        |
+--------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
